decision: Probe both the normal and fault-only qrexec coordinator services with authenticated read-only stats requests before launching the multi-run qualification campaign, and bind recovery manifests to those same deployment service names.
problem: The qualification runner previously probed only the normal coordinator service. A missing or mis-routed fault-only qrexec service could therefore remain undetected until committed-response-loss campaigns had started. In addition, recovery manifests hard-coded dig.CoordinatorFault, so a custom fault service could pass preflight but the campaign could still invoke a different service.

reviews.preferred: dual-service authenticated preflight plus manifest binding
reviews.reason: It proves both services used by qualification are reachable and authenticated, and guarantees the recovery campaign consumes the same normal/fault service configuration that was probed.

reviews.preferred: read-only stats probes through existing signed envelopes
reviews.reason: The probes preserve the existing HMAC and qrexec policy boundaries, do not mutate mission state, and keep the fault-only service separate from the normal service.

reviews.preferred: two bounded preflight round trips before long-running campaigns
reviews.reason: The extra fault-service stats round trip is materially cheaper than entering a campaign with a 31 second lease-expiry wait or multiple recovery runs when the fault service is unavailable.

alternatives.rejectedBecause: Does not validate the separate fault-only service required by recovery qualification.

alternatives.approach: Probe normal and fault services and bind campaign manifests to the same deployment configuration
Dedicated health/attestation daemon for both services
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Adds a new long-lived service, policy surface and lifecycle before the existing qrexec protocol requires it.

qa: Reject missing or malformed deployment bindings and transport secrets.
Require source and target Qubes to differ and normal/fault qrexec service names to differ.
Require successful authenticated stats responses with valid timing evidence from both normal and fault-only services.
Fail closed when either service rejects authentication, returns malformed stats, or cannot produce valid timing evidence.
Materialize recovery campaign normal/fault service fields from the same validated deployment configuration used by preflight.
Run preflight and qualification-runner tests inside the distributed-faults CI shard and npm test.
lessons: A preflight is only useful if it exercises every service the qualification sequence will actually invoke.
Hard-coded service names can silently break the equivalence between what preflight validates and what the campaign executes.
Failing early with two read-only qrexec probes is cheaper and diagnostically cleaner than discovering policy or service mistakes during fault injection.
